Traditional demand forecasting methods in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) supply chains increasingly prove inadequate for mitigating demand variability driven by supply disruptions, market volatility, and complex risk factors. While machine learning (ML) and supply chain risk management (SCRM) have emerged as distinct optimization strategies, empirical evidence integrating the two remains limited. This study examines whether ML-enhanced SCRM improves demand forecasting accuracy in FMCG operations. Using a sequential mixed- methods design, we conducted semi-structured interviews (n = 7 companies) and administered a structured survey (n = 55 professionals; 58.5% response rate) across Egyptian FMCG firms. Multiple regression analysis revealed that both ML integration (β = 0.20, p < .05) and SCRM maturity (β = 0.35, p < .01) significantly predict forecast accuracy (R² = .21, F(3,116) = 10.23, p < .001). Mediation analysis (Sobel z = 2.15, p < .05) confirmed that SCRM partially mediates the relationship between ML-forecast accuracy and the outcome. Cronbach’s alpha coefficients demonstrated strong internal consistency across constructs (α = .83-.89). Findings underscore that ML efficacy requires complementary risk governance structures; standalone algorithmic implementation yields…

fmcg.title: Predicting Purchase Behavior in Fast-Moving Consumer Goods: Micro-Moment Intent Prediction Framework
fmcg.authors: Independent Researcher, USA, Mr. Pratik Khedekar
fmcg.venue: International journal of data science and machine learning.
fmcg.abstract: This research presents the Temporal-Contextual Micro-Moment Prediction Framework (TCMP), an innovative approach for forecasting Fast-Moving Consumer Goods purchas- ing behavior that mitigates significant deficiencies in current pre- dictive approaches. The system uses advanced machine learning algorithms to combine data from several sources, such as social media sentiment, real-time behavioral analytics, and traditional transaction data, to forecast purchase intent over several time periods. The study addresses three fundamental gaps in current FMCG predictive analytics: temporal granularity limitations that focus on either immediate or long-term predictions without capturing intermediate decision phases; micro-moment context integration challenges that treat consumer interactions as isolated events rather than connected sequences; and real-time feature engineering constraints that create prediction lag in dynamic market environments. The study makes important theoretical progress in predicting consumer behavior over multiple time periods and gives useful frameworks for putting the ideas into practice in the actual world. Some of the most important new ideas are streaming feature computation techniques, cross- platform social media integration methodologies, and privacy- preserving analytics approaches that keep predictive efficacy while following the rules. These…

fmcg.title: Investigating of Dominant Factors Causing Loss of Sales and Marketing in a Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) Company in Lagos
fmcg.authors: A. Eghuruamrakpo, O. O. Johnson
fmcg.venue: Ijagun Journal of Social and Management Sciences
fmcg.abstract: The Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) sector contributes substantially to Nigeria's national economy, yet the sector has experienced declining sales performance in recent years, reducing revenues for key market players. While prior studies have examined the sector broadly, few have investigated sales losses within individual firms. This study examined the primary factors driving lost sales and marketing underperformance at Nestlé Nigeria, with a focus on Lagos, and aimed to provide evidence-based insights to support improved competitive performance. A mixed-methods design was used, combining quantitative and qualitative approaches. Quantitative data included inventory levels, stock-out frequencies, marketing campaign metrics, sales figures, consumer demographics, and macroeconomic indicators. Qualitative data were gathered through surveys, focus groups, and customer interviews. Analysis employed frequency distributions, means, standard deviations, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and correlation analysis. High competition and poor customer service were the most frequently cited internal contributors to sales loss. PCA identified ineffective marketing strategies (loading = 0.671), poor customer service (loading = 0.265), and insufficient product availability (loading = 0.138) as the dominant internal factors. Among external influences, competitor pricing strategies (Mean =…

fmcg.title: Forecast Value Add: Reward-Based Action Selection over Probabilistic Demand Forecasts
fmcg.authors: Ankur Verma
fmcg.abstract: Strong machine-learning ensembles capture much of the trend, seasonality, and known events in demand, yet they can still understate peaks, miss moving events, or mistake temporary changes for shifts in demand level. We address this gap by framing forecast refinement as a reward-driven decision problem. For each forecast period, we let an agent choose among values already produced by the ensemble: its base forecast, distribution-free bounds, quantiles, and a bias-corrected estimate. We evaluate these choices against context-matched historical periods, accounting for calendar position, recurring and moving events, trend, price, and promotions. We then apply a structural seasonal guard to constrain adjustments and record the model, agent, and planner contributions to every published value. We evaluate our approach across five retail, consumer-goods, and direct-to-consumer deployments over nine months. Our refined forecasts reduce mean WMAPE by 6.3% compared with the stacked machine-learning forecast for every customer, with gains reaching 16.7%, and achieve the lowest error in 35 of 45 customer-months. Compared with statistical forecasts, our approach reduces mean error by 18.7%. These results demonstrate that context-aware, auditable action selection can add forecast value beyond a strong ensemble.

fmcg.title: TimeHF 2.0: Multimodal, Multivariate, and Multi-Region Collaborative Forecasting for Large-Scale Retail Supply Chains
fmcg.authors: Zhongxuan Han, Zhengxin Shi, Kunxiu Chen et al.
fmcg.abstract: Large-scale retail supply chains need sales forecasts for specified products, future dates or planning windows, and regions under the conditions available at the forecast origin. Regional sparsity, changing environments, volatile sales, and unfamiliar business situations make these dimensions difficult to model together. We introduce TimeHF 2.0, a multimodal, multivariate, and multi-region collaborative forecasting framework that makes flexibly expressed business knowledge usable in numerical prediction. A coverage-aware directed encoder integrates regional sales and applicable covariates. A semantic alignment module transfers language-model hidden representations of natural-language plans and domain experience into target-specific forecasting context. Learning against sales observations connects these meanings to numerical evidence, allowing business users to supply experience, future plans, and changing circumstances without defining a new numerical feature for each description. Text-conditioned future queries and shared/routed experts adapt prediction to the supplied context. An ordered-distribution head allocates fine resolution to routine fluctuations and coarse resolution to extreme sales movements, while daily/window learning connects forecasts to cumulative planning quantities. Online parallel forecasting at JD yields relative accuracy improvements of 18.25% and 17.94%…

fmcg.title: Fuzzy selective state model for forecasting the dynamics of consumer preferences
fmcg.authors: P. A. Golovinski, A. A. Drobyshev, A. O. Shatalova
fmcg.abstract: We consider forecasting the dynamics of consumer preferences of retail chain customers. A customer's preference is described by a triangular fuzzy number. The evolution of the preference over time is governed by a Mamba-type selective state space model whose hidden state is a triangular number, with computations carried out in M.G.~Matveev's two-component algebra of fuzzy numbers. The recurrence parameters are computed from crisp features, while the fuzzy part of the model remains linear with non-negative coefficients. We show that the state then always remains a proper triangular number and is a convex combination of past observations, so that the fuzziness of the forecast does not accumulate over time and the algebraic computations coincide with Zadeh's extension principle. On a synthetic example with competitor promotions and customer switching, a lightweight 107-parameter model reaches a mean absolute error of the forecast centre of 0.154 versus 0.163 for the constant-inertia evolution operator and 0.179 for the naive forecast, matches a crisp model of the same architecture and additionally provides a linguistically interpretable estimate of forecast vagueness. We also show how the linguistic readout of the forecast can be used to detect a permanent switch of a customer to a competitor.

fmcg.title: FARE: Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion for Retail Forecasting
fmcg.authors: Chenghao Gu, Zhuokang Shen, Shenghao Wu et al.
fmcg.abstract: Retail sales forecasting underpins inventory planning, yet promotions and calendar events reshape short-term demand. Although each factor usually has historical occurrences, the complete factor combination of a target week often has few precedents. The challenge is therefore to retrieve informative partial matches and weight them by their reliability, which varies across series. We propose FARE(Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion), which ranks historical weeks separately for each known target-week factor and merges the selected weeks into a factor reference under a fixed budget. Guided by shrunk errors from completed development weeks and the current disagreement among candidates, a first gate mixes this factor reference with a shape reference from similar sales histories, and a second gate controls how strongly the mixture corrects a backbone forecast. Both gates remain fixed during testing. On Favorita, M5, Rossmann, and Rohlik, FARE reduces the weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) of five backbones by 11.46%, 4.06%, 14.63%, and 10.16% on average. With Chronos-2 frozen, FARE also outperforms conventional and existing enhancement methods, including supervised residual correction and retrieval augmentation. Code is available at https://github.com/HousonGu/FARE .

fmcg.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Quantile Demand Forecasting in E-commerce with Doubly Censored Data
fmcg.authors: Ziwen Ye, Jiawen Wei, Teng Song et al.
fmcg.abstract: In recent years, a growing number of online retail companies have embraced deep learning models for demand forecasting, leveraging their scalability in processing large-scale datasets. Accurate demand forecasts enable improved planning and allow operational flexibility to adjust sales accordingly. Moreover, quantile estimation has gained widespread application as it offers valuable uncertainty quantification, thereby enhancing the robustness of decision-making processes. However, limited research has addressed the effective quantification of uncertainty when target labels are ambiguous. In retail, actual sales can be capped by stock and boosted by temporary promotions, whereas the target is underlying demand. Such scenarios are characterized by double censoring and no deep-learning pipeline yet exists for such data. In this paper, we introduce a straightforward framework for learning quantiles from doubly-censored observations and propose a tailored evaluation metric. Our approach is supported by theoretical guarantees, and we empirically demonstrate that our metric correlates well with the oracle calibration measure. Experimental results show that our estimator surpasses existing baselines. Finally, inventory simulations and real-world applications confirm the practical utility of our method in retail operations.

fmcg.title: TimeWorld: Towards Action-Conditioned Multimodal World Models for Time Series Forecasting
fmcg.authors: Hang Ni, Weijia Zhang, Hao Liu
fmcg.abstract: Time series forecasting supports decision-making in web applications such as online retail and network management, where planned actions can reshape future dynamics. World models provide a natural paradigm for predicting such action-dependent changes beyond extrapolating historical patterns. However, existing time series world models (TSWMs) typically rely on fixed, domain-specific covariate schemas that limit flexible intervention specification, while multimodal forecasters treat text primarily as passive predictive context. To investigate these gaps, we introduce TSWM-Bench, a cross-domain benchmark for multimodal TSWMs spanning seven real-world datasets, with textual interventions grounded in recorded action--outcome data. Our evaluation reveals that conventional multimodal forecasters underperform history-only time series foundation models (TSFMs) despite dataset-specific training, whereas simple text-prefix adaptations improve forecasting across all evaluated TSFM backbones. These findings suggest that pretrained TSFMs encode implicit world knowledge of temporal dynamics, offering a strong foundation for action-conditioned modeling beyond conventional multimodal fusion. Building on this insight, we propose TimeWorld, a plug-in framework that adapts pretrained TSFMs through explicit action-response modeling. Specifically, the Prototype-Guided Latent Modulation (PLM) module…

fmcg.title: World Models, Trees and Foundation Models for Retail Forecasting: Evidence from Four Public Data Sets
fmcg.authors: Karthik Iyer, Madan Dabbeeru
fmcg.abstract: A retailer makes different decisions at different grains of the product, store and time hierarchy: store orders for an item in a store, supplier funding for an item across stores, category performance by store, and the financial plan for the chain. Which forecasting model to use depends on the grain. This paper compares models at each grain on four public data sets (M5, six Dominick's categories, Breakfast at the Frat, and Corporación Favorita, the last kept out of all development), over rolling forecast origins with paired tests and model confidence sets. It covers price and promotion through the plan inputs these data record, not product, assortment or place. The models are a world model that carries each item's state forward under the price and promotion plan, the same network without that state, LightGBM, the Temporal Fusion Transformer, TimesFM, Chronos-Bolt, Timestral, seasonal naive, and an equal-weight average of the world model, LightGBM and TimesFM given the plan. The answer changed with the grain. For an item by store and an item across stores, the average had the lowest error on seven and eight of nine data sets, and the 90% confidence set held a median of 1 and 2 models. For a category by store, a category and the chain total, the lowest-error model differed between data sets and a median of 4 of nine models were not separated by the four to six windows available.…

fmcg.title: EvoCast: Reliable Autonomous Research Agents for Iterative Forecasting Architecture Evolution
fmcg.authors: Kaipeng Xu, Xianli Yan, Yan Wang et al.
fmcg.abstract: Deep time-series forecasting models have rapidly diversified, yet adapting them to a specific task still requires extensive expert effort in model selection, mechanism diagnosis, architecture design, implementation, and evaluation. Existing AutoML methods are constrained by predefined search spaces, while general-purpose LLM research agents lack reliable control over experimental protocols and model promotion. We introduce EvoCast, a fully autonomous research-agent system for iterative forecasting architecture evolution. EvoCast first establishes and diagnoses a task-specific baseline through executed mechanism ablations, then generates evidence-grounded research directions from dataset characteristics, diagnostic results, prior rounds, and failure records. Its central design, cognition-authority separation, assigns open-ended hypothesis generation and code implementation to LLM agents, while deterministic program authorities control source-edit boundaries, canonical evaluation, and promotion decisions. Experimental outcomes are accumulated as evidence to guide subsequent rounds. Results show that EvoCast completes complex architecture modifications with higher implementation success and lower agent-side token/time cost, and develops task-specific architectures that outperform selected baselines, strong forecasting models, and agent baselines in three real-world forecasting…

fmcg.title: LLM-enhanced spatio-temporal learning for grid-level docked bike sharing demand prediction
fmcg.authors: Xuxilu Zhang, Francesc Soriguera
fmcg.abstract: Short-term bike-sharing demand forecasting is complicated by spatial-temporal non-stationarity and the practical difficulty of incorporating unstructured external text into numerical pipelines. Conventional approaches rely on historical flow sequences and fixed graph structures, thereby constraining their accuracy when anomalous social events perturb normal travel patterns. We propose a forecasting framework in which a Large Language Model (LLM) drives a semantic shockwave mechanism that converts free-form urban text, such as municipal event schedules, local news, and transit bulletins, into quantified spatial-temporal perturbation fields. The LLM extracts three physically interpretable parameters per event (intensity, spatial reach, and temporal lag), from which Gaussian decay fields are constructed and injected into a Zero-Inflated Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (ZI-ASTGCN). To handle the pronounced sparsity of grid-level measurements, the model couples a dual-branch output head with a multi-task zero-inflated loss that jointly trains a gating probability and a conditional flow intensity. Experiments on the operational Barcelona Bicing dataset show that ZI-ASTGCN outperforms established neural baselines, with particularly strong gains during high-demand periods, validating the utility of physics-grounded semantic signals in spatial-temporal mobility…

fmcg.title: ProtoFlow: Prototype-Guided Flow Matching for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
fmcg.authors: Shibo Feng, Wanjin Feng, Yang Qiu et al.
fmcg.abstract: Generative modeling has shown strong promise for multivariate time mseries (MTS) forecasting, especially scale to high-dimensional settings. Diffusion-based methods achieve competitive performance but typically require many sampling steps at inference. VAE-based non-iterative forecasting frameworks have therefore emerged as an efficient alternative. Within this line of work, vector quantization (VQ) enables controllable latent space modeling by mapping multivariate series into compact discrete representations. Existing VQ-based forecasting methods, however, typically rely on autoregressive (AR) token generation, which suffers from exposure bias and training-inference mismatch. Flow matching provides an efficient non-autoregressive alternative for latent forecasting, but existing formulations usually initialize transport from a generic Gaussian prior. We instead observe that the trained VQ codebook already captures representative latent prototypes and can thus serve as a more informative prior for flow matching. Based on this insight, we propose ProtoFlow, a forecasting framework that combines vector-quantized autoencoding with Prototype-prior Flow matching. Our method first maps multivariate sequences into a discrete latent space, then constructs a structured prior from the learned codebook, and finally learns a DiT-based rectified flow to transport samples from this prior to…

fmcg.title: Historical Anchors for Scientific Forecasting on Human-Aware Knowledge Graphs
fmcg.authors: Siu Tin Wu, Ryan C. Barron, Phoebe Upton Sanderbeck et al.
fmcg.abstract: Predicting which scientific connections will form next can point researchers toward the most promising leads. One successful approach learns representations by sampling paths through publication networks, represented by a hypergraph, that connect scientific entities, concepts, and researchers, approximating how knowledge and expertise move through the literature. Sampled paths are then used to train an embedding model to forecast scientific connections such as a property of a material. Performance, however, depends strongly on how many paths are sampled: too little sampling yields incomplete representations, while further sampling can eventually weaken prediction quality. The best sampling budget is therefore often identifiable only after future discoveries are known. We introduce Query--Anchor Agreement (QAA), a diagnostic requiring no future labels or separately trained model. QAA can be used to select a sampling budget, and refine or re-rank the resulting forecast to improve forecasting scientific connections. QAA compares the candidates a model predicts for a target with those most similar to the target's known historical examples, and identifies when these two views converge. Across thermoelectric-material and COVID-19 drug-repurposing benchmarks, repeated random-seed runs, and three sampling policies, QAA-selected budgets fall on average 1.86 percentage points below…

fmcg.title: Dynamic factor and double PCA models for partially observed survival curves: Forecasting demand in short-term rental markets
fmcg.authors: Marthe Elisabeth Aastveit, Alex Lenkoski, Thordis Thorarinsdottir
fmcg.abstract: This paper develops prediction models for population-level survival curves observed over time and sampled from a heterogeneous mix of populations. We consider a discrete-time setting where each curve is only partially observed and forecasts of the remaining trajectory are needed for downstream decision making. Our approach recasts cross-population heterogeneity into a multivariate sampling model. We propose two forecasting models for partially observed curves: a full factor analysis model that extends a general factor representation to incorporate the partially observed survival curve, and a double PCA model. The methodology is motivated by demand forecasting in short-term rental markets, where market-level occupancy paths can be viewed as survival curves over the booking horizon and where forecasts of future occupancy feed into dynamic pricing algorithms. We apply the models to the newly released Wheelhouse dataset, which contains time series of market occupancy curves for 500 markets from 2017 to 2022. Model performance is assessed using the integrated quadratic distance, and we compare the proposed PCA-based methods to Holt's linear trend model across multiple forecast horizons. The results show that the proposed models yield accurate and stable forecasts of the remaining survival trajectory and generally outperform Holt's method, particularly at longer horizons.

markets.title: Stock Market Forecasting: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods
markets.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
markets.abstract: Stock market forecasting is a challenging task due to the highly dynamic, nonlinear, and volatile nature of finan-cial markets. This research presents a comparative analysis of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques for stock price prediction. The study focuses on data preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, and performance evaluation using historical market data. Various algorithms are analyzed based on accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. The findings highlight the strengths and limitations of each approach, providing insights into selecting appropriate models for real-world financial applications

markets.title: Stock Market Forecasting Trends and Price using Different Machine Learning Techniques: Systematic Review
markets.venue: Journal of Kufa for Mathematics and Computer
markets.abstract: Financial stock markets play a significant role in supporting the economy by enhancing market liquidity, facilitating risk-sharing, minimizing the costs of financing, and contributing to the capital market. These functions offer more opportunities for economic growth. Stock market forecasting of prices or trends is a critical endeavor for investors and financial institutions to mitigate risk, optimize returns, and improve portfolio management. To address these challenges, numerous approaches have been proposed, involving time series forecasting, machine learning models, deep learning, ensemble techniques, and hybrid forecasting, which enhance the accuracy and reliability of forecasts. This study provides a systematic review of the literature on stock market forecasting, highlighting methodologies through comparative tables.

markets.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Quantitative Finance and Stock Market Forecasting
markets.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
markets.abstract: This study investigates the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in quantitative finance, financial technology, and stock market forecasting. Emphasizing their ability to manage large datasets and improve financial predictions, the research details the entire methodology, including data collection, preprocessing, model selection, simulation, and outcome analysis. Linear regression models, particularly suited for stock price prediction, are used alongside Python libraries such as Scikit-learn and TensorFlow to facilitate large-scale implementation. The study also evaluates other models, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and Decision Trees, applied to tasks like stock price forecasting and credit risk classification. Results demonstrate that AI and ML significantly enhance financial forecasting accuracy and improve portfolio management. Furthermore, this research highlights the strengths and limitations of current techniques and suggests potential advancements through the integration of AI with technologies such as blockchain and quantum computing. Future directions include exploring these emerging technologies to further increase efficiency and innovation in the financial sector.

markets.title: Machine learning in stock market forecasting: a comprehensive review
markets.authors: Moksh Khemka, Kamal Haddad, Tanzim Redwan et al.
markets.abstract: Forecasting financial markets remains difficult because price series are noisy, nonlinear, nonstationary, and subject to structural breaks. This structured review synthesizes empirical machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) research on equities, indices, commodities, foreign exchange, and cryptocurrencies, covering classical ML, recurrent networks, CNN-based models, attention and Transformer architectures, multimodal and graph-based systems, and reinforcement-learning approaches. Because studies differ in task formulation, horizon, data frequency, target variable, feature set, validation design, and metric choice, the review combines qualitative synthesis with structured quantitative evidence mapping rather than a single pooled effect size. The paired-error aggregation identified 17 peer-reviewed studies and 47 same-dataset, same-horizon proposed-versus-baseline error comparisons. On a study-level median basis, this subset showed a median relative error reduction of 20.3%, with an interquartile range of 5.7%-50.7% and a full range of −0.8%-71.5%. These results indicate that ML/DL methods often improve reported performance in controlled experiments, but they do not establish universal real-world superiority. Comparability remains limited by validation design, transaction costs, slippage, market regimes, and inconsistent uncertainty reporting. Future work should prioritize…

markets.title: Stock Price Prediction Using Machine Learning
markets.venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
markets.abstract: Abstract—Forecasting stock market prices is a challenging task for traders, analysts, and engineers due to the myriads of variables influencing stock prices. However, the advent of artificial intelligence (AI) and natural language processing (NLP) has significantly advanced stock market forecasting. AI’s ability to analyze complex data sets allows for more informed predictions. Despite these advancements, stock price forecasting remains an area where AI has not yet achieved optimal results. In this paper, we forecast stock prices using 30 years of historical data from various national banks in India sourced from the National Stock Exchange. We employ advanced deep learning models, including multivariate multi-step Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Facebook Prophet with LightGBM and Optuna, and Seasonal Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA). Additionally, we analyze news data from tweets and reliable sources like Business Standard and Reuters, recognizing their significant impact on stock price movements. Index Terms—Stock Market Forecasting, Data preprocess- ing, Advanced Algorithms, Deep Learning Models, Multivari- ate Multistep LSTM, SARIMA, LightGBM, Optuna, acebook Prophet,Sentiment Analysis.

markets.title: A Systematic Literature Review of Machine Learning Methodologies in Stock Market Forecasting
markets.authors: Priyanka Ramchandra Mali and Dr. K. G. Sawarkar
markets.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
markets.abstract: Stock market prediction remains one of the most compelling yet elusive challenges in computational finance due to the inherent volatility, non-linearity, and chaotic nature of financial time-series data. In recent years, the paradigm has decisively shifted from traditional statistical econometrics toward data-driven artificial intelligence. This paper presents a systematic literature review exploring the evolution, methodologies, and architectural frameworks of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) applications in stock forecasting over the past decade. We establish a comprehensive taxonomy to evaluate existing research across three critical pillars: data input dependencies (technical, fundamental, and alternative textual data), algorithmic variations (shallow models, ensemble tree-based methods, sequential networks like LSTM, and advanced hybrid optimization systems), and performance evaluation metrics. Furthermore, this review shifts away from generic algorithmic summaries to critically examine persistent gaps in the literature that hinder the real-world deployment of these predictive frameworks. Specifically, we examine the systemic issues of data snooping and model overfitting, the "black box" interpretability dilemma within deep architectures, and the frequent omission of practical transaction costs and slippage parameters in backtesting environments. By…

markets.title: NeuroStock: A Deep Learning Framework for Stock Market Forecasting with Web-Based Analytics
markets.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
markets.abstract: Stock market prediction is challenging due to its volatile, nonlinear nature. NeuroStock is a deep learning framework using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Hybrid CNN-LSTM models to predict stock prices over 7-60 days. It processes real-time Yahoo Finance data and evaluates performance with metrics like RMSE, MAE, R2, Directional Accuracy, and Precision. A Streamlit web app lets users select stocks, tweak settings, view predictions, and compare models. Tests on GOOG stock show the Hybrid CNN-LSTM model balances accuracy (RMSE: 9.218274, R2: 0.913406), while LSTM minimizes errors (RMSE: 4.413391). Unlike prior studies, NeuroStock excels in model comparison, trend prediction, and user-friendly deployment. It offers real-time insights for investors and analysts. Future updates, like sentiment analysis and additional data inputs, will boost accuracy, making NeuroStock a powerful tool for financial forecasting.

markets.title: Machine Learning And Stock Return Prediction: Evidence From The Nigerian Emerging Markets
markets.authors: Omoregbe Osas Imade, Muhammad Lawal Alfa
markets.venue: International Journal of Accounting Management and Economic Review
markets.abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of machine learning techniques in predicting stock returns in the Nigerian stock market. Using daily stock prices from 2015 to 2024, the study examines the predictive power of technical indicators (RSI, MACD, Moving Averages, Momentum), market variables (trading volume, market returns, volatility), and macroeconomic factors (interest rate, inflation, exchange rate). Machine learning models, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were implemented with hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation to ensure robustness. Results indicate that technical indicators are the most influential predictors, with RSI and MACD showing the highest importance. Ensemble models, particularly XGBoost, achieved superior predictive accuracy, outperforming single models in out-of-sample tests. Market variables contributed moderately, while macroeconomic factors played a secondary role in short-term prediction. The study concludes that combining technical indicators with advanced machine learning models provides a reliable framework for forecasting stock returns in volatile emerging markets like Nigeria. The findings offer practical insights for investors, portfolio managers, and policymakers seeking to improve decision-making using data-driven approaches.

markets.title: Stock Price Prediction Using Machine Learning Technique
markets.abstract: This project presents a novel approach to stock price prediction using machine learning techniques, with a specific focus on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Utilizing real-time dataset from Tata Motors spanning the last five years, the study aims to forecast the closing stock prices accurately. The project encompasses data pre-processing, dataset splitting, LSTM model implementation, and evaluation of prediction accuracy. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of LSTM in predicting stock prices, achieving approximately 80% accuracy. The research contributes to the field of finance and machine learning by showcasing a practical application of LSTM in stock market forecasting. The project adheres to academic standards and ensures originality, making it suitable for publication without plagiarism concerns.

markets.title: Stock Market Prediction Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
markets.venue: Journal of Recent Innovation in Science and Technology
markets.abstract: Stock market prediction has emerged as one of the most challenging and important research areas in finance and artificial intelligence. Accurate prediction of stock prices enables investors, financial institutions, and policymakers to make informed investment decisions and manage financial risks effectively. Traditional statistical forecasting models have shown limited performance due to the nonlinear, dynamic, and highly volatile nature of financial markets. In recent years, Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques have significantly improved prediction capabilities by learning complex relationships from historical market data, technical indicators, fundamental information, and textual sentiment extracted from news and social media. This review systematically examines recent developments in stock market prediction, focusing on traditional statistical models, machine learning algorithms, deep learning architectures, hybrid approaches, reinforcement learning, and transformer-based models. The paper also discusses commonly used datasets, evaluation metrics, challenges, and future research directions. The review provides researchers with a comprehensive understanding of current methodologies and emerging trends in intelligent financial forecasting.

markets.title: Stock Price Prediction Using Machine Learning: Research Paper Directions
markets.venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
markets.abstract: Stock market investment strategies are complex and rely on an evaluation of vast amounts of data. In recent years, machine learning techniques have increasingly been examined to assess whether they can improve market forecasting when compared with traditional approaches. The objective for this study is to identify directions for future machine learning stock market prediction research based upon a review of current literature. A systematic literature review methodology is used to identify relevant peerreviewed journal articles from the past twenty years and categorize studies that have similar methods and contexts. Four categories emerge: artificial neural network studies, support vector machine studies, studies using genetic algorithms combined with other techniques, and studies using hybrid or other artificial intelligence approaches. Studies in each category are reviewed to identify common findings, unique findings, limitations, and areas that need further investigation. The final section provides overall conclusions and directions for future research. Keywords: machine learning, stock market prediction, literature review, research taxonomy, artificial neural network, support vector machine, genetic algorithm, investment decision

markets.title: Intelligent Stock Price Prediction Based on Historical Financial Data and Machine Learning
markets.venue: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science
markets.abstract: Forecasting stock prices sits at the intersection of machine learning and financial data analysis and it has drawn serious attention from researchers in recent years.The financial markets produce enormous volumes of transactional records every single day, and buried within that data are signals that, with the right tools, can hint at where prices might be heading.This study draws on several key market variables -including opening and closing prices, intraday highs and lows, and daily trade volumes -to build a working prediction framework.Rather than relying on manual interpretation, we apply machine learning methods that can surface nonobvious relationships in the data and produce forecasts that go well beyond what conventional approaches offer.The work walks through each phase of the development pipeline, from gathering and cleaning data, all the way through to model training, prediction, and evaluation.We also take an honest look at both the opportunities this approach unlocks and the real limitations it faces.Ultimately, the findings show that thoughtful application of machine learning can be a genuine asset for investors and market analysts who want to ground their decisions in data rather than intuition.

markets.title: Literature Review on Stock Price Predictions with reference to Machine Learning Approaches and Statistical Methods
markets.abstract: An Indian stock market is an open market where businesses and individuals can increase revenues. Organizations use the stock market to buy and sell shares. The interest rate and the supply of shares determine the cost of shares. Trading/exchanging refers to purchasing and selling shares. Only Listed Companies are permitted to do so. Vast sums of money have recently been traded on stock exchanges worldwide. National economies are intricately linked, and the performance of their stock exchanges has a significant impact. As a final outcome, they are connected with macroeconomic variables and have a more direct impact on everyday life. They form a mechanism with critical and urgent social consequences as a natural outcome. Investors who trade stocks must have access to timely information in order to make wise decisions. Additionally, stock price behavior is unpredictable and challenging to forecast. These factors make stock price forecasting a critical and hard process to find the value of a particular share. This paper highlights the various research aspects applied to stock price predictions of shocks using machine learning approaches and statistical methods.

markets.title: Systematic Literature Review: Stock Price Prediction Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
markets.abstract: In order to determine the type of evaluation with the attributes utilised, the methods employed, the methods most frequently used, and the methods with the greatest performance, this research was carried out using a literature review method to analyse various studies. Based on pre-established criteria, 40 publications were selected from research conducted between 2016 and July 2021 for this study. Four research topics estimation, classification, clustering, and association—were determined by this review. Four research topics fundamentals, technical, sentiment analysis, and even a combination with analyses that make use of their respective qualities and datasets—are the results of this study. Thirty-one different methods have been identified for stock price prediction. The most popular approaches are LSTM, MLP, RF, and SVM. Furthermore, MLP is a technique that yields the best results, with an LSTM of 70% and a performance of 71.63%. For better precision, it is advised to employ deep learning, ensemble approaches, mixed machine learning, and input attribute selection at pre-processing.

markets.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Stock Price Prediction
markets.abstract: Machine learning models are becoming more popular for predicting stock prices. Their advanced algorithms often perform better than traditional statistical methods. This study aims to carry out a bibliometric analysis using VosViewer. It focuses on the number, variety, and connections of studies related to stock price prediction using Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests, and Deep Learning techniques. Boolean operators were used to search for and filter relevant articles from the Dimensions database. We conducted a manual review to select only high-quality studies, resulting in 55 peer-reviewed articles for analysis.The analysis highlights important trends, influential studies, and collaborative networks in the field. This provides a clear overview of how machine learning models are developing for stock price prediction. There has been a notable rise in publications since 2013, with major contributions from institutions in the United States, the United Kingdom, India, and China. Emerging themes, especially deep learning applications, have been identified. However, there is still a lack of in-depth academic evaluation of these models.This study stresses the need for more empirical research to address algorithmic biases and improve model reliability. The findings offer useful insights for researchers and practitioners, guiding future studies and helping to develop more…

markets.title: A Review and Taxonomy on Deep Learning Models for Forecasting Stock Market Trends
markets.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
markets.abstract: Machine learning is transforming stock market prediction by leveraging vast datasets, advanced algorithms, and computational power to provide more accurate forecasts. While challenges remain, continuous advancements in artificial intelligence and deep learning are improving predictive models, making them an essential tool for traders and investors. Stock market prediction extremely challenging due to the dependence of stock prices on several financial, socio-economic and political parameters etc. For real life applications utilizing stock market data, it is necessary to predict stock market data with low errors and high accuracy. This needs design of appropriate artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) based techniques which can analyze large and complex data sets pertaining to stock markets and forecast future prices and trends in stock prices with relatively high accuracy. This paper presents a comprehensive review on the various techniques used in recent contemporary papers for stock market forecasting.

markets.title: Deep learning in factor investing: an application to Indonesian Islamic and conventional equities
markets.authors: Muhammad Ghazali Ash Shiddiqie, Mohsin Ali
markets.venue: International Journal of Islamic and Middle Eastern Finance and Management
markets.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the efficacy of integrating machine learning (ML) architectures and feature selection protocols within a traditional asset pricing framework to enhance equity return predictability. Design/methodology/approach Leveraging a methodological pipeline that synergizes artificial neural networks (ANN) with sequential feature selection (SeFS) and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regularization, this study analyzed the momentum, value and quality risk premia across 949 conventional and 621 Islamic equities in the Indonesian market from 2016 to 2025. To isolate robust signals, this study further uses complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) for price denoising. Findings Empirical results indicate that momentum factors, particularly those with a one-month horizon, exhibit superior predictive power. Feature selection consistently identifies one-month momentum, earnings-to-price and gross profit-to-total assets as primary predictors. Notably, Islamic equities exhibit greater sensitivity to valuation anomalies, with EBIT/EV and gross profit-to-enterprise value providing additional predictive power. The ANN models achieve robust forecasting performance, with forecasting performance metrics ranging from 70% to 85%. The predictive outcomes exhibit significant invariance to the number of hidden layers,…

markets.title: A Review on Artificial Intelligence-Driven Stock Market Forecasting: Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
markets.venue: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science
markets.abstract: This review aims at reviewing the emerging trend associated with the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to support financial forecasting in the stock market. Traditional methods for financial prediction such as technical analysis and time-series modeling have several flaws in terms of the inability to accurately estimate financial indicators in a nonlinear, highly volatile market environment. On the contrary, the use of machine learning-based approaches is characterized by higher efficiency and scalability. Several popular approaches such as deep learning models, reinforcement learning (adaptive trading strategy development), natural language processing for sentiment analysis, and machine learning-based algorithms can be used in stock market forecasts. Advantages and disadvantages of these techniques are critically analyzed, and the emphasis is placed on ways to overcome the limitations associated with traditional forecasting techniques and increase predictive performance. In specific, the quality of data, different information sources, data preprocessing procedures, as well as key metrics are considered for evaluating models and their performances. Specific cases will be discussed in detail, and current limitations, including interpretability, dependency on data, and model opacity, will be outlined. Finally, future trends for research in this area will be highlighted.

markets.title: Advancements in Stock Price Prediction: Integrating Statistical, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Models
markets.venue: International Journal on Science and Technology
markets.abstract: Forecasting stock prices has been a persistent challenge and focal area of research due to the volatile and complex nature of financial markets. Traditional statistical methods provided early insights into market behaviors, while recent advancements in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have enabled improved predictive accuracy through data-driven modeling. This paper reviews a broad spectrum of stock price forecasting methods across three major categories: statistical models, machine learning approaches, and deep learning architectures. We examine the theoretical foundations, performance, advantages, limitations, and real-world applications of each method. Additionally, a comparative analysis highlights the evolving landscape and the increasing integration of hybrid and ensemble techniques. This review includes references from seminal and recent works in the field.

markets.title: Machine Learning Return Prediction for Enhanced Investment Portfolio Analysis in Emerging Markets
markets.abstract: This study addresses the challenge of improving investment portfolio performance in emerging financial markets, where high volatility and structural instability often limit the effectiveness of traditional forecasting approaches. The main objective is to enhance stock return prediction and portfolio allocation by applying advanced machine learning techniques to the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, Africa’s largest and most liquid equity market. The Johannesburg Stock Exchange is selected due to its representative role among emerging markets and its exposure to sectoral concentration, market inefficiencies, and macroeconomic shocks. The analysis covers the period from 2004 to 2024, allowing the model to capture multiple market cycles, including periods of stress and recovery. The empirical analysis is based on daily stock price and trading volume data for nineteen highly liquid firms, complemented by firm-level financial indicators obtained from established financial databases. The research employs a recurrent neural network framework designed for sequential data, incorporating both market-based indicators and firm fundamentals, alongside rigorous data preprocessing and rolling-window validation. The findings confirm that the proposed hybrid modeling approach improves return predictability and leads to superior risk-adjusted portfolio performance compared with conventional…

markets.title: Stock price prediction based on dual important indicators using ARIMAX: A case study in Vietnam
markets.authors: Pai-Chou Wang, Tram Thi Hoai Vo
markets.abstract: Vietnam’s stock market is characterized as a frontier market and focuses on emerging market status by 2025. Tisco Advisory’s report showed that Vietnam’s stock market is expecting to draw 4 billion in foreign capital in 2024. Despite the appealing nature of the stock market, forecasting stock prices remains a complex endeavor owing to its fast-paced and fluctuating volatility. Effectively forecasting the fluctuation of stock prices has the potential to mitigate the risk associated with stock investments and enhance the overall investment yield. In this research, we combine the advantages of XGBoost for feature selection with the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMAX) time series model for forecasting to improve the accuracy of predicting next-day stock prices. A dual important features selection approach is proposed to extract key features for the ARIMAX model from a pool of 87 technical indicators. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, we compared it with four other methods – long-short term memory, genetics algorithms with long-short term memory, XGBoost, and Meta Prophet – in predicting the next day’s closing price of the Vietnam stock index from January 2013 to April 2023. The results indicate that the performance of our method is better than others and suitable for traders to make stock investment decisions.

markets.title: Machine Learning-Based Stock Return Prediction: Evidence from the Saudi Arabian Stock Market (Tadawul)
markets.abstract: Return predictability on the Saudi Arabian Stock Exchange (Tadawul), the largest equity market in the Middle East, remains underexplored relative to its structural distinctiveness as an oil-linked, retail-dominated emerging market. We compare 11 predictive models spanning five linear (regularised) regressors, three tree-based ensembles, and three stacked hybrid architectures. This comparison quantifies the improvement that nonlinear and ensemble methods offer over linear benchmarks for daily return prediction in this setting and identifies which method delivers the best accuracy-versus-cost trade-off for practical deployment. Using 28,750 daily observations (January 2015–December 2025), we constructed a 40-feature technical signal space spanning six families and evaluated all 11 models under a strict chronological train–validate–test protocol with an 18-month sealed holdout. A Lasso–XGBoost stacked ensemble achieves the lowest test RMSE of 0.906 and an out-of-sample Information Coefficient of 0.133, outperforming linear benchmarks by 15–27% in forecast error. Translated into a long-short strategy subject to 0.6% round-trip transaction costs, the optimal model delivers a Sharpe ratio of 0.587, an 81.1% win rate and a maximum drawdown of −5.53% across 758 trades. Sensitivity analysis confirms robustness across hyperparameter grids and rolling estimation windows. Bollinger Band…

markets.title: Exploring Machine Learning Methods for Stock Market Prediction: A Review
markets.authors: Deepak D. Kapgate, Soni A. Chaturvedi
markets.venue: International Journal of Advances in Engineering and Management
markets.abstract: Stock market prediction has long been a challenging and highly dynamic field due to the inherent volatility and complexity of financial markets. Traditional methods, such as auto regressive models and moving averages, have limitations in capturing the non-linear, everchanging behavior of stock prices. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful tool, offering the ability to analyze large volumes of data and uncover hidden patterns. This paper presents a comprehensive review of various machine learning techniques, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and hybrid models, focusing on their application in stock market prediction. We examine the strengths, weaknesses, and challenges of these techniques and suggest directions for future research. The paper concludes by discussing potential avenues for improving predictive accuracy, particularly through the integration of advanced deep learning models, real-time data processing, and sentiment analysis.

markets.title: From Data to Decisions: Evaluating Machine Learning Models for Stock Market Forecasting
markets.authors: Yashodhan Karulkar, Arshi Shah, Rishab Naik
markets.abstract: Predicting trends in the financial markets remains a demanding yet crucial responsibility undertaken by market participants and financial professionals. This research quantitatively evaluates how effectively machine learning algorithms anticipate outcomes in stock price forecasting for five major Indian companies: Reliance Power, Hindustan Unilever, State Bank of India, Tata Motors, and Nestle. By integrating traditional statistical techniques, including simple moving average (SMA) and exponential moving average (EMA), with supervised learning algorithms such as logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and linear discriminant analysis (LDA), this study provides a comparative analysis of model effectiveness. The empirical findings reveal that classification-based models exhibit varying degrees of predictive efficacy. LDA correctly classified 65% of original grouped cases, surpassing the minimum required accuracy of 63.37%. KNN achieved a higher accuracy of 75%, outperforming LDA. Logistic regression demonstrated an improvement from the intercept model’s 55.9% accuracy to 57.1% in Block 1 model, indicating that incorporating meaningful variables enhances prediction reliability. Additionally, EMA proved to be more responsive to price volatility, effectively capturing short-term fluctuations compared to SMA. The results provide meaningful understanding into the strengths…

markets.title: Fine-Tuning an Order-Flow Foundation Model for Sub-Second Forecasting
markets.abstract: Generative models have become the standard approach in language and vision. These models are typically pretrained first and then fine-tuned. Recent work demonstrates how to pretrain an autoregressive generative model on Level-3 order-flow data. However, to our knowledge, no one has fine-tuned such a model yet for downstream tasks. Here we first pretrain a 300M-parameter generative model on Level-3 order-flow data collected from two crypto exchanges, Bitstamp and Bitfinex. Then we fine-tune the pretrained model to predict the microprice return and its realized volatility. We show that our fine-tuned model outperforms classical baselines, such as gradient boosting on handcrafted features, in predicting microprice returns over sub-second horizons. Furthermore, the predictive ability of the model transfers zero-shot to assets it was never fine-tuned on. Due to the short-term nature of these forecasts, the predicted microprice moves are smaller than the bid-ask spread plus fees, so the natural applications are in execution and market making. These results indicate that a pretrained generative model can be turned into a competitive short-horizon price forecaster via fine-tuning.

markets.title: Tabular Foundation Models in Financial Predictions
markets.abstract: This technical note introduces tabular foundation models (TFMs) to accounting research and evaluates their performance in one common benchmark task: predicting firms' next-year earnings changes. TFMs produce numeric predictions and learn in context, without post-release training or tuning, making them natural and easy to use for forecasting. The TFMs we study are pretrained on synthetic tabular data, so they avoid look-ahead bias from memorizing firms' outcomes. We compare Google Research's TabFM with a fine-tuned open-weight large language model developed in recent accounting research and with several tree-based models. TabFM is more accurate than all comparison models. It is also faster and less computationally intensive than the large language model. Several tree-based specifications produce predictions more quickly than TabFM, so choosing between them involves a trade-off between accuracy and speed. We conclude that TFMs have promise as a new tool for forecasting in accounting and finance. However, our evaluation is based on a single benchmark task, and no class of models is likely to dominate in all settings.

markets.title: Diversification Across Predictors: Heterogeneous Ensemble Learning for Cross-Sectional Return Prediction
markets.abstract: Cross-sectional stock return prediction remains challenging due to extremely low signal-to-noise ratios, high-dimensional factor spaces, and non-stationary predictor effectiveness. Individual model classes exhibit complementary failure modes in this regime: neural networks overfit noise due to high variance, while linear models underfit nonlinear structure due to high bias. We propose a heterogeneous ensemble framework that extends the financial principle of diversification to the predictor level. Through a bagging procedure combining linear predictors with nonlinear predictors, each model functions as a distinct specialist whose prediction errors exhibit low cross-covariance, enabling error cancellation upon aggregation. We formalize this mechanism via bias-variance-covariance decomposition, establishing an exact mathematical correspondence between portfolio diversification and predictor aggregation. On CSI300 daily-frequency Alpha158 factor datasets, the proposed ensemble achieves a Rank IC improvement exceeding 13\% over standalone neural networks and surpasses tree-based state-of-the-art methods including XGBoost and Double Ensemble, as measured by both predictive accuracy and portfolio-based evaluation metrics.

markets.title: Neural Realized Measures: Forecast-Supervised Intraday Aggregation for Volatility Forecasting
markets.authors: Brian Sing Fan Chan, Jennifer So Kuen Chan
markets.abstract: High-frequency volatility forecasting typically separates measurement from prediction: intraday observations are first compressed into a daily realized measure using a fixed aggregation rule, and the resulting statistic is then passed to a forecasting model. This conventional pipeline therefore treats measure construction as forecast-agnostic preprocessing. We ask whether the aggregation stage itself can instead be learned from the downstream forecasting objective while preserving the statistical structure of established realized measures. We propose Neural Realized Measures (NRM), a primitive-preserving, forecast-supervised aggregation framework that retains the original measure-specific intraday contributions but replaces uniform aggregation with positive, mean-normalized context-dependent weights. Uniform weights exactly recover the corresponding raw realized measure (RRM), so the classical construction is nested as a special case. Because NRM remains an explicit weighted sum of established primitive contributions, it also retains direct bar-level attribution. Across SF, HAR, and MIDAS forecasting specifications, NRM is evaluated against corresponding RRM specifications under controlled comparisons. In Heston simulations, NRM reduces RMSE for both contemporaneous and next-day latent integrated variance across all evaluated primitive--regime combinations. On six…

markets.title: Beyond Anonymous Order Flow: Wallet Identity as a Feature for Short-Horizon Return Prediction
markets.abstract: Conventional public order-book data summarize trading without identifying the accounts behind it. Hyperliquid's Level-4 record also exposes persistent pseudonymous wallet addresses. We reconstruct full-depth books from consensus-ordered messages and evaluate wallet identity as a feature for short-horizon return prediction. The July 1-27, 2026 record covers 17.1 billion messages, 14.3 million aggressive orders by 147,113 wallets, and $84.3 billion in taker notional across ten markets. In the three model markets, notional-weighted ten-second markout rankings persist across adjacent ten-day windows (Spearman rho = 0.52); covariate-adjusted validation markouts reach 3.11 basis points in the top ventile. On a 100-millisecond grid, eleven features describing previously scored top-decile wallets raise one-second out-of-sample R2 from 10.88% to 12.

markets.title: Safe Portfolio Learning from Untrusted Predictions: Signed Trust, Abstention, and Cross-Universe Polarity Failure
markets.authors: Amirhossein MohammadpourAzari, Mohammad Zarei, MohammadAmin Fazli
markets.abstract: Portfolio use of machine predictions must often proceed while the predictions' economic direction, reliability, and timing remain untrusted, and while feedback from overlapping multi-period positions arrives with delay. A controller chooses among Safe, Follow, and Reverse portfolio actions, so signal orientation is learned rather than assumed. A share-adaptive master updates action probabilities from matured Safe-relative rewards, an evidence gate can abstain by transferring unsupported directional probability to Safe, a delayed collateral budget reserves worst-case loss capacity before exposure is funded, and a protected split account caps the capital adaptive decisions may touch. The architecture carries a dual certificate, tracking regret against switching action sequences under delay and one-sided intervention, together with a pathwise collateral safety bound that holds when predictions fail. On a 24-stock development universe a conservative prediction-assisted overlay stays near equal-weight performance at a fraction of the turnover. On a frozen 82-stock holdout, the pre-specified Reverse orientation fails to outperform Equal Weight; a separately labeled post-holdout diagnostic shows that permanently flipping the sign to Follow also does not recover a return edge. Under the post-holdout controller, protected wealth remains within 15.9 basis points of the Safe benchmark…

markets.title: Aggregate Calibration Can Mask Stress-State Undercoverage: Bounded-Memory Forecast Intervals under Recurrent Financial Stress
markets.abstract: Sequential forecast intervals are often evaluated by aggregate coverage even when calibration memory is bounded. This can be misleading when economically important states recur after long absences: a recent-only buffer may satisfy its overall coverage target while no longer containing errors from earlier episodes of the returning state. We study this problem in next-day financial range forecasting, holding the forecasting model, conformity score, adaptive update, and memory budget constant while varying the historical residual information available at each query. Recent-only first-in, first-out (FIFO) calibration is near nominal in aggregate but undercovers substantially during high-volatility states in both an exchange-traded fund development panel and a fixed stock panel. An unbounded state-history reference yields a lower observed stress-period interval score; Rare replay yields lower high-VIX interval scores than the matched Recent-n and Hybrid-n controls in both panels, and the state-structured versus recent-only contrast is largest near stress re-entry. Bounded calibration memory is therefore part of the forecasting information design, and aggregate calibration alone can conceal state-specific reliability failures.

markets.title: Evaluating LLM Research Agents as Tests of Return Predictability
markets.abstract: Researchers ask large language model research agents whether a forecasting model beats the historical-mean benchmark, a question that real data cannot settle. We evaluate the agent's verdict as a statistical test in runs of three commercial models and one open-weight model in simulated return series whose predictive signal, if any, is known. The commercial agents detect weak signals more often than an out-of-sample test, mainly because they accept weaker evidence: held to an agent's false-positive rate, a conventional in-sample test does as well or better. All four models claim predictability too often when no signal exists; the commercial agents also state miscalibrated probabilities and change their verdicts after a sentence about prior research. Magnitudes vary by model; excess false claims persist without a resampling artifact. Agent verdicts are informative but need a neutral brief, a decision rule fixed outside the agent and a sealed holdout.

markets.title: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting
markets.authors: Renáta Rusnáková, Eugen Šlapak, Gaurav K. Pandey et al.
markets.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) processes temporal information through quantum dynamics, but it remains unclear whether small QRC models can forecast real data competitively with classical models and whether their predictions survive the transfer from ideal simulation to noisy hardware. We address both questions for a six-qubit gate-based reservoir that forecasts next-day motor-insurance claim counts. Five reservoir candidates were selected and frozen using hardware-native interaction graphs, Trotterized Ising dynamics, memory and measurement-robustness criteria, circuit cost, and calibrated-noise screening. On 232 held-out test days, the ideal candidates reached root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 5.66-6.12 claims/day, compared with 5.36 for ridge regression. For four of the five, the difference from ridge was not significant under a 95% block bootstrap, and their accuracy was comparable with classical recurrent and reservoir baselines. On the 156-qubit IBM Kingston processor, we ran 63 evaluations in 21 paired rounds, comparing hardware-aware, random-native, and Qiskit optimization level 1 layouts. Hardware-aware placement gave lower RMSE than Qiskit in every round, with a maximum transfer distortion of 7.59 claims/day (11.84 for Qiskit), and avoided the severe transfer failures seen for some random layouts. Most of the hardware distortion appeared as a systematic forecast…

markets.title: Interpretable Allocation and Model-Predictive Rebalancing of Equity Portfolios, Tested on Real and Synthetic Markets
markets.abstract: A live equity portfolio poses three problems: which stocks to hold, when to trade, and whether the strategy holds up beyond the observed market. We built one system for all three and tested it on 373 US equities, calibrated on 2014-2024 and traded from January 2025 to September 2026. A selection rule chose stocks by score, by a bandit, or at random, and one of seven weighting rules, four consumer-theory utilities, and three standard portfolios, set share counts under limits on budget, single-stock weight, portfolio volatility, and turnover, with each stock's preference weight a bounded score of its trend, market beta, and the market's recent direction. A model-predictive controller forecasts portfolio value with a multi-asset geometric Brownian motion and re-planned at its horizon, when the value left its forecast band, or at a drawdown stop. To probe deeper declines than the real window held, we also ran the system on simulated markets from per-asset hidden Markov generators with jumps, linked by market and sector factors. markets.title: TensorLOB: Structure-Preserving Tensor Learning for Limit Order Book Forecasting
markets.abstract: The limit order book (LOB) records outstanding buy and sell orders across multiple price levels. Its state evolves over time across market side, price level, and order attribute, naturally forming a multiway structure. However, existing LOB models typically flatten these dimensions into a matrix model, thus obscuring the existing structural relationships. Starting from first principles and the market-microstructure intuition of the LOB, we design TensorLOB to operate entirely in the tensor domain. TensorLOB uses mode-wise tensor contractions for feature extraction and directly contracts the learned representation with low-rank class-weight tensors for prediction, retaining the distinct roles of time, side, level, and attribute modes. Experiments on the FI-2010 benchmark show that TensorLOB achieves the highest accuracy, recall, and F1 score across all four evaluated horizons. This proof of concept highlights the potential of high-dimensional modelling of multi-way latent information intrinsic to financial markets, which has so far been largely overlooked.

markets.title: Reading the Count: Prediction Markets and Brazil's 2026 Presidential Election
markets.abstract: We rebuild the public count of Brazil's 2026 presidential runoff minute by minute from the electoral court's section-level records and compare it with every trade on Kalshi and Polymarket. A projection published live on the night gave the eventual winner, Lula, a probability of 0.998 from 19:15, with 1.6% of sections counted. The markets reached 0.9 at 20:24, with 46% counted. Read as the projection's central estimate with a wider uncertainty, their prices imply a standard deviation of the final margin about four times the live projection's, and about twice that of a section-level projection calibrated on the 2018 runoff, the earlier night with the largest errors. Valued at these projections, takers' purchases of Lula after the count resumed had an expected profit of 4 to 18 cents per Kalshi contract after fees; valued at a state-level extrapolation of the count, it was zero. During a two-hour suspension of the count the markets gave Lula 0.25 to 0.44, below every reading we compute afterwards from the sections then public, none of which was available live. On the first-round night, when the headline count showed the eventual leader ahead from its first file, the same markets were faster than our projection.

logistics.venue: Frontiers in Business Economics and Management
logistics.abstract: As the world's largest warehouse membership retailer, Costco's successful operation and management model has attracted much attention. This paper conducts an in-depth study on Costco's operation and management model, and analyzes its characteristics and advantages in supply chain management, inventory management, logistics management, and employee management. The research results show that Costco's operation and management model is centered on efficient supply chain management, lean inventory management, flexible logistics management, and motivated employee management, achieving low-cost and high-efficiency operations. At the same time, this paper also explores the replicability and limitations of Costco's operation and management model, providing reference and reference for other companies.

logistics.title: Operations at Flipkart Supply Chain Management
logistics.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
logistics.abstract: This research paper explores the operations of Flipkart's supply chain management system, focusing on its structure, strategies, and technological innovations. As one of India's largest e-commerce platforms, Flipkart has built a highly responsive and efficient supply chain network to handle vast product assortments, fluctuating demand, and complex logistics. This paper aims to analyze how Flipkart manages procurement, inventory, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery while maintaining customer satisfaction and operational efficiency. The study also sheds light on the company's sustainability initiatives and the future of e-commerce logistics in India

logistics.title: Supply Chain Management Practices And Their Impact On Operational Efficiency In Retail Enterprises
logistics.venue: Manuscript on Sustainable Economics Finance and Management
logistics.abstract: Effective supply chain management (SCM) is increasingly critical to the competitiveness and operational efficiency of retail enterprises. This study examines how SCM practices procurement processes, inventory management, supplier collaboration, logistics & distribution, and information systems influence operational efficiency in organized retail in Karnataka. Adopting a mixed-methods approach, the study draws on a structured survey of 400 store managers/operations staff across five Karnataka cities (Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubli–Dharwad, Belagavi) and 15 in-depth interviews with supply-chain managers and suppliers. Quantitative analysis uses descriptive statistics, ANOVA, and multiple regression; qualitative data were analysed by thematic coding. Results indicate that improved inventory management (higher inventory turnover, lower stockouts), integrated IT systems (real-time inventory visibility), and closer supplier collaboration (joint planning, vendor-managed inventory pilots) significantly predict higher operational efficiency (measured via order fulfilment rate, reduced lead time, and lower supply-chain cost per sale). Logistics infrastructure and state-level initiatives have supported improvements, but fragmentation in last-mile distribution and supplier heterogeneity remain constraints. logistics.title: Assessing The Impact Of AI-Automation In Supply Chain Management
logistics.abstract: Artificial intelligence nowadays stands among the most powerful transformative forces of modern times for supply chain management. It opens a new avenue towards automation, optimization, and better decision-making. This dissertation seeks to explore how AI-driven automation impacts supply chain processes in an industrial context with respect to influences on operational performance, inventory control, and stock optimization. The study therefore has a mixed-methods character, as it encompasses not only quantitative data from questionnaires, but also qualitative insights provided through in-depth interviews with professionals across diverse industries-manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, among others. Results indicate that AI technologies like predictive analytics and machine learning algorithms with robotic process automation enhance efficiency in supply chains, reduce costs, and make better decisions. This study also attempts to make a case for the presence of major challenges, including technical integration problems, an initial high cost, and lack of confidencea in data privacy. This dissertation discusses the transition toward AI automation in supply chain management and takes a close look at the feasibility and practicality of AI tools to optimize inventory management and distribution logistics. Using in-depth interviews with key stakeholders from all walks of industry…

logistics.title: Autonomous Mobile Robots in Logistics and Supply Chain Management of Industry 4.0, A Review
logistics.abstract: Industry 4.0 has revolutionized supply chain management and logistics through a concentration on automation, data interchange, and smart technologies. Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) is advanced robotic applications in industry 4.0 which can provide flexibility, efficiency, and scalability in supply chain management. So, the integration of AMRs in advanced manufacturing, could provide cost-effectiveness production, and consumer satisfaction. AMRs can minimize delays by lowering reliance on humans, and guaranteeing real-time flexibility in response to customer demand fluctuations. Their unmatched flexibility, adaptability, and scalability in warehouse tasks like picking and sorting are made possible to function without predetermined routes and human involvement. Furthermore, by maximizing the usage of resources and minimizing negative environmental effects, AMRs play a crucial role in promoting resilience and sustainability. Thus, challenges from e-commerce expansion, sustainability concerns, and supply chain disruptions can be managed by using ARMs in part manufacturing. This review explores the role of AMRs in logistics and supply chain management within the industry 4.0 paradigm. Key topics in the study are ARMs integration with IoT, AI, and digital twins; optimization of operations such as order picking, inventory management, and last-mile delivery. Also, challenges and…

logistics.venue: Krakow Review of Economics and Management/Zeszyty Naukowe Uniwersytetu Ekonomicznego w Krakowie

It aims to fill a research gap by offering an objective overview of the latest advancements in decision-making techniques and their impact on supply chain performance. Research Design & Methods: The paper employs a systematic literature review to examine the application MCDM techniques in supply chain management. The review follows a five-step process: 1) formulation of research questions, 2) identification of relevant studies through the Scopus database, focusing on English-language journal articles published between 2006 and 2023, 3) selection and evaluation of studies using structured keyword searches and content screening, resulting in a final sample of 348 peer-reviewed articles, 4) analysis and synthesis of the selected literature in relation to the research questions, and 5) reporting the findings to identify research gaps and suggest future research directions. Findings: The review reveals the diverse applications of MCDM tools and models in addressing complex supply chain challenges, including demand forecasting, inventory management, distribution optimisation, and risk assessment.
