logistics.title: Transforming Supply Chain Management with Next-Generation Technology (AI, Drones and Robots)- A Bibliographic Review
logistics.venue: Journal of Information Systems Engineering & Management
logistics.abstract: The global supply chain is undergoing a radical transformation driven by emerging technologies such as robots, drones, and artificial intelligence (AI). These (modern technologies) are redefining supply chain management by enhancing efficiency, reducing operational costs, and improving resilience against disruptions such as natural disasters, geopolitical tensions, and pandemics. AI-driven predictive analytics have significantly optimized demand forecasting, inventory management, and decision-making processes, leading to a more responsive and agile supply chain ecosystem. This paper explores the profound impact of these next-generation technologies, analysing their contributions to supply chain optimization, logistics enhancement, and real-time monitoring as well examine the critical challenges associated with their implementation, including cybersecurity risks, regulatory constraints, data privacy concerns, and ethical considerations related to workforce displacement. logistics.title: Unleashing the power of big data analytics in supply chain management: a strategic roadmap through systematic literature review
logistics.authors: Umar Nawaz Kayani, Mirzat Ullah, Oleg S. Mariev et al.

logistics.venue: Journal of Critical Care & Emergency Medicine
logistics.abstract: Background: Efficient Supply Chain Management (SCM) is critical for ensuring timely and safe surgical care, particularly in resource-constrained settings. This study investigated the impact of SCM practices, including inventory management, procurement efficiency, demand planning, and logistics and distribution, on surgical outcomes at Mpilo Central Hospital, Zimbabwe. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 83 healthcare professionals, including surgeons, nurses, anesthetists, and inventory managers, achieving a 92% response rate. Traditional optimization techniques often fail to address uncertainties in demand, logistics disruptions, and the need for trust among stakeholders. Inspired by the Namib desert beetle’s fog-harvesting ability—where hydrophilic and hydrophobic surface patterns maximize water collection from scarce resources—this study introduces a Fog-Harvesting Inspired Optimization Algorithm (FHIOA) for supply chain management. The algorithm mimics the beetle’s adaptive strategy by integrating selective absorption and directional flow mechanisms into a computational framework that enhances resource allocation, inventory management, and distribution planning. To strengthen trust and data integrity across stakeholders, FHIOA is integrated with blockchain technology, enabling immutable transaction records, real-time visibility, and decentralized coordination. logistics.title: Big Data Empowering Supply Chain Management: From Theory to Practice
logistics.abstract: With the rapid development of the digital economy, big data technology has brought unprecedented opportunities for supply chain management. This paper takes Shenzhen Shemanquban Supply Chain Co., Ltd. as a case study to explore the application and effects of big data technology in supply chain management. logistics.title: Trends in AI-Based Supply Chain Management: A Text Mining Analysis of Academic Literature
logistics.abstract: This study examines research trends in the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and its impacts within the field of supply chain management (SCM). A total of 1,663 academic articles published since 2000 that investigate AI applications in SCM were analyzed using network text analysis and topic modeling techniques. The results reveal that the integration of AI into supply chain management has generated positive effects on traditional supply chain performance indicators, such as improved demand forecasting accuracy and enhanced inventory and logistics management. In addition, AI adoption has shown significant implications for supply chain sustainability and resilience. The analysis identifies four major research topic groups associated with AI-based supply chain management: (1) core technologies, (2) sustainability enhancement, (3) resilience building, and (4) security and ethical issues. By systematically structuring the existing body of research, this study provides a comprehensive overview of the evolving AI-SCM research landscape and offers directions for future research.

logistics.title: Application Of Mathematical Modeling In Supply Chain Management: A Review
logistics.authors: Norazryana Mat Dawi, Mohammad Akhtar, HAMIDREZA NAMAZI
logistics.abstract: Mathematical modeling plays a critical role in modern supply chain management (SCM) by enabling optimization, forecasting, and informed decision-making across complex networks. This review synthesizes recent advancements in mathematical modeling across five key domains of SCM: demand forecasting, inventory control, logistics and distribution, sustainability, and the integration of emerging technologies. We explore a wide array of modeling techniques, including time-series analysis, stochastic models, optimization algorithms, and machine learning, highlighting their applications, strengths, and limitations. Special attention is given to the evolving roles of artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and digital twins in enhancing model responsiveness and adaptability. Despite these advancements, challenges remain in achieving model transparency, scalability, and seamless integration with real-time technologies such as IoT and digital twins. Future research should focus on developing more interpretable machine learning models, improving data governance, and fostering cross-domain collaboration to enhance decision-making across the supply chain. This review provides a foundational understanding while identifying key gaps and future pathways for innovation in mathematical modeling for supply chain management.

logistics.title: The Impact of Using AI in Supply Chain on Corporate Management

logistics.abstract: As the current market becomes increasingly competitive and labor costs continue to rise, enterprises must explore alternative strategies to enhance their supply chain management for better development and innovation. The main study in this research paper is the potential impact of AI on improving supply chain efficiency. Key components of the supply chain include information processing, inventory management, logistics management and customer feedback. This study focuses on the practical applications of existing AI technologies in supply chain management. The main features are to fasten and animate order data processing, improve order accuracy, simplify and accelerate inventory processes, optimize express delivery routes, and improve customer satisfaction. In addition, AI applications in supply chain management can significantly reduce work time costs and reduce labor costs, enabling companies to develop rapidly and gain a competitive edge in the market.

logistics.title: Differentiable Agent-Based Modeling for Multi-Echelon Supply Chains: Gradient-Based Optimization of Heterogeneous Policies at Scale
logistics.authors: Bulent Soykan, Murtadha Alsayegh, Sean Mondesire et al.
logistics.abstract: Global supply chains rely on the interactions of thousands of heterogeneous agents, posing significant challenges for optimization. While traditional optimization often assumes homogeneity to ensure tractability, Reinforcement Learning struggles with sample inefficiency when scaling to high-dimensional state spaces. We propose a Differentiable Agent-Based Model for multi-echelon inventory management. By implementing stochastic dynamics via differentiable tensor operations, we enable direct gradient propagation through the simulation. We validate the framework by recovering theoretical Newsvendor optima without supervision. Crucially, we demonstrate ``Mass Personalization'' by optimizing 10,000 distinct agent policies simultaneously in seconds, achieving a 53% cost reduction compared to scalar baselines. Furthermore, we utilize gradient sensitivity analysis to generate causal heatmaps, accurately recovering inherent lead-time delays from the computation graph. This approach bridges the gap between simulation and optimization, enabling the efficient training of self-correcting Digital Twins.

logistics.title: TimeHF 2.0: Multimodal, Multivariate, and Multi-Region Collaborative Forecasting for Large-Scale Retail Supply Chains
logistics.authors: Zhongxuan Han, Zhengxin Shi, Kunxiu Chen et al.
logistics.abstract: Large-scale retail supply chains need sales forecasts for specified products, future dates or planning windows, and regions under the conditions available at the forecast origin. Regional sparsity, changing environments, volatile sales, and unfamiliar business situations make these dimensions difficult to model together. We introduce TimeHF 2.0, a multimodal, multivariate, and multi-region collaborative forecasting framework that makes flexibly expressed business knowledge usable in numerical prediction. A coverage-aware directed encoder integrates regional sales and applicable covariates. A semantic alignment module transfers language-model hidden representations of natural-language plans and domain experience into target-specific forecasting context. Learning against sales observations connects these meanings to numerical evidence, allowing business users to supply experience, future plans, and changing circumstances without defining a new numerical feature for each description. Text-conditioned future queries and shared/routed experts adapt prediction to the supplied context. An ordered-distribution head allocates fine resolution to routine fluctuations and coarse resolution to extreme sales movements, while daily/window learning connects forecasts to cumulative planning quantities. logistics.title: LLM-Based Feature Extraction for Multi-Criteria Inventory Classification
logistics.abstract: E-commerce supply chains generate large volumes of customer feedback and operational data that remain underutilized in inventory management. Traditional inventory classification techniques such as ABC analysis rely primarily on annual dollar usage, while multi-criteria inventory classification (MCIC) methods extend this but still depend on structured quantitative data and do not utilize unstructured information available in modern supply chains. This paper proposes an LLM-based feature extraction approach that transforms unstructured sources such as customer reviews into quantitative features using vector embeddings and LLM-generated evaluation criteria. The enriched feature set is incorporated into an MCIC framework based on the Hadi-Vencheh model. Experimental results show measurable reclassification effects when customer sentiment signals are included, demonstrating that integrating unstructured data into MCIC can enhance inventory prioritization.

logistics.title: Cross-Border Ownership and Input Access: Evidence from the Lithium Supply Chain
logistics.abstract: How does cross-border ownership shape the lithium supply chain? Using global data on mines and refineries, I estimate a model in which ownership can lower refiners' effective ore costs, encourage mines to restrict spot sales, and soften competition. To study these effects, I examine policies motivated by national security concerns about reliable access to critical mineral inputs: divestiture of Chinese stakes in overseas producers and a ban on ore exports to China. Divestiture increases spot ore supply but leaves lithium output nearly unchanged, while continued trade preserves Chinese access to ore. The export ban reduces global lithium supply because refining capacity elsewhere cannot fully replace lost Chinese production. Ownership transfers do not reserve ore for domestic production; restricting Chinese access imposes a substantial supply cost at existing capacities.

logistics.title: Distributionally Robust Dynamic Inventory Control: Automatic Recovery under Martingale Demand
logistics.authors: Jianzhi Leng, Daniel Zhuoyu Long, Lun Ran et al.
logistics.abstract: Problem definition: We study dynamic inventory control for battery-swapping stations that combine central replenishment with automatic local recovery. Central replenishment improves immediate battery availability but reduces the depleted-battery pool available for subsequent recovery, creating an intertemporal trade-off. Managing this trade-off is particularly challenging when historical demand data are limited and future demand is uncertain and temporally dependent. Methodology/results: We develop a time-consistent distributionally robust dynamic program under martingale demand ambiguity, using the latest observed demand as the next conditional mean without requiring a fully specified demand distribution. We establish an optimal order-up-to policy for every finite horizon and identify two critical recovery rates governing replenishment decisions. Under a regular penalty condition, we derive explicit finite-horizon policies and worst-case demand distributions, showing that sufficiently strong automatic recovery makes central replenishment unnecessary in nonterminal periods. Extensions to submartingale and supermartingale demand reveal contrasting behaviors, including eventual full-capacity replenishment under upward ambiguity and recovery-induced positive replenishment under downward ambiguity. logistics.title: Palimpsestic Accountability in the US Federal AI Inventories
logistics.authors: Dipto Das, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Aditya Vashistha et al.
logistics.abstract: An AI inventory is a structured, often public record in which a government or organization lists and describes the AI systems it uses or plans to use. Studies of single AI inventory releases describe what systems do but say little about how they are governed over time. We linked entries across three releases of the US Federal AI Use Case Inventory (2023--2025), compared answers only where both releases required them, and analyzed governance accounts through a dual deductive-inductive approach, guided by the Algorithmic Decision-Making Adapted for the Public Sector (ADMAPS) framework. As the inventory grew from 710 to 3,611 entries from 2023 to 2025, fewer required answers were left blank, but accountability was rewritten through three mechanisms. Each release \emph{redrew} the scope of the questions; agency-assigned classifications \emph{gated} what was reported; and answers were also \emph{overwritten}, with gains and losses concentrated in single agencies and little account of human oversight and judgment. These findings show that each release redraws the boundary of accountability and leaves the public to \emph{re-stitch} the records, a condition we term \textbf{palimpsestic accountability}. We recommend versioned records, reasons for every reclassification, public files that distinguish kinds of missing answers, and oversight documented as conditions to improve public…

logistics.title: Late Autumn: LLM Agents Specialize a General Multi-Robot Planner for One Warehouse
logistics.authors: Yimin Tang, Han Zhang, Shao-Hung Chan et al.
logistics.abstract: No algorithm is best on all problems, but a real warehouse is a narrow problem: its layout and processes rarely change. Operators still run one general multi-robot planner at many sites, because experts cannot tune it for each one. In this work, which we call Late Autumn, we explore whether LLM coding agents running autonomous research can specialize a general planner for one site, trading generality for throughput, much as post-training adapts a pretrained LLM to one task. We study six campaigns on a lifelong planner that combines task assignment with multi-agent path finding, on a floor modeled on an existing automated warehouse. We find that (1) the agents raise throughput by 22--60%, and the gains hold on unseen seeds; (2) they rediscover known MAPF mechanisms, such as corridor-exit priorities, local guidance, and rollouts, and independent campaigns find the same bottleneck; (3) the gains largely carry over to another layout, a larger fleet, and other service times, shrink with a smaller fleet, and mostly vanish under an outbound-heavy demand mix; and (4) each final patch (0.7k--2.4k lines) is a chain of scored commits with a median step of 27 lines, so experts can review it, and review finds problems that the score misses; some patches multiply planner compute by over 100x. LLM agents can therefore turn each site's bias into extra throughput at little engineering cost,…

logistics.title: Halal-NeSyNet: Clause-Scoped Neuro-Symbolic Cross-Attention for Automated Food Ingredient Auditing and Risk-Aware Halal Logistics Triage
logistics.authors: Mochamad Rizal Fauzan, Naila Nursyifa, Irgi Surya
logistics.abstract: Verifying that a packaged food is Halal requires reading ingredient declarations and E-number additives before goods enter certified warehouses. Dual-origin additives such as E471, E422, E441 and E920 are Mushbooh (doubtful) unless a botanical, microbial or certified-Halal qualifier appears in the same ingredient clause, so a plant-based qualifier on one clause must not clear an unqualified additive in another. We call a failure to respect this scope cross-clause modifier confounding and build a benchmark of 3,199 items (277 Open Food Facts records and 2,922 template-generated clause-swap items, labelled by an explicit 50-code rule base rather than by a certification authority) with a 540-item counterfactual suite. We propose Halal-NeSyNet, which couples a DistilBERT encoder with a 16-dimensional rule-derived symbolic vector through cross-attention and gated fusion, trained with an asymmetric false-Halal risk loss. Over five seeds, text-only TF-IDF baselines reach 86.25-86.71 % accuracy with 13.42-21.73 % false-Halal leakage and 6.33-26.00 % counterfactual triad consistency, whereas Halal-NeSyNet reaches 97.04+/-0.34 % and 99.67+/-0.50 %. Gradient boosting given the same symbolic vector reaches 96.25+/-1.24 % (+0.59 points from Halal-NeSyNet, 95 % CI [-1.11, +2.28]), so most of the gain comes from clause-scoped symbolic features and not from the network, and the risk loss did…

logistics.title: Improved Approximation Guarantees for Periodic-Review Stochastic Inventory Control
logistics.abstract: In periodic-review stochastic inventory control, replenishment policies must balance holding and backlogging costs while responding to uncertain demands and evolving forecasts that may be arbitrarily correlated and nonstationary. In this general information setting, Levi, P{á}l, Roundy, and Shmoys (Mathematics of Operations Research 2007) established that the fully adaptive optimum can be approximated within factor $2$, which had remained the best-known performance guarantee since then. Their marginal cost accounting and dual-balancing framework made this comparison possible without computing optimal decisions across future trajectories, opening a broad research program on approximation algorithms for stochastic inventory systems. We break this long-standing barrier for periodic-review stochastic inventory control, showing how to compete against the fully adaptive benchmark within factor $\frac{ e }{ e-1 } \approx 1.582$ while retaining general demand correlations and evolving forecasts. We attain these advances by discovering a structural connection between marginal inventory accounting and weighted stopping problems, where each unit's conditional holding charge forms a supermartingale, while postponing its order incurs a history-dependent backlog charge. To leverage the random thresholding approach of Ma and Tzamos (ICML 2023) in this context, we develop a potential-function…

logistics.title: Quantum Vehicle Routing Problem: a smart initialization strategy for ill-conditioned optimization landscapes
logistics.authors: Emanuele Casciaro, Mario De Simone, Stefano Martina et al.
logistics.abstract: With the expansion of complex transport infrastructure, new paths for linking different destinations have emerged, allowing the definition of multiple routes. The introduction of new roads may also lead to disruptions in traffic flow. This problem can be generalized into a special case of VRP, which aims to find the optimal route for a fleet of vehicles within a network of destinations. Finding solutions to this problem requires an exponential number of operations, hindering the ability of exact solvers to deal with large instances, which must therefore be tackled using heuristics, often leading to suboptimal results. Quantum-based algorithms may allow us to find exact solutions in polynomial time with high probability, offering a potential future alternative to classical solvers and in this work, we focus on the QAOA. Our novel contributions are a parameter-initialization strategy that improves the convergence probability and the integration of the subtour constraints directly into the optimization without using additional qubits by employing an approximation of exponential equality constraints. We believe that our results pave the way for effectively solving instances of VRP using quantum-based solutions, leveraging the space-efficient problem encoding and our initialization strategy, which limits the effect of barren-plateau under random parameter initialization.

logistics.title: Carbon-Aware Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Decision-Focused Learning
logistics.authors: Jaume Reixach, Wanru Chen, Jiaming Wu et al.
logistics.abstract: Electric vehicles produce no tailpipe emissions, but charging them produces emissions that depend on the time-varying generation mix of the electricity consumed. We study an Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with a carbon-aware objective that accounts for charging-related emissions alongside conventional routing costs. The problem determines routing, charging, and waiting decisions, allowing charging demand to be shifted toward periods with lower grid carbon intensity. Because these decisions depend on forecasts of future carbon intensity, we propose a decision-focused learning approach so that the training of the model employed for predicting the carbon intensity of the grid over time is solver-aware. In particular, we train a linear predictor using approximate SPO+ directions and employ a time-limited Large Neighborhood Search followed by exact postprocessing as the underlying solver. Experiments on realistic Germany-based instances show that explicitly considering charging-related emissions reduces realized emissions by 28.76% on average relative to carbon-blind optimization, although at the expense of higher non-carbon operating cost. Moreover, decision-focused training reduces realized total cost by 2.30% on average relative to conventional prediction-focused learning and performs better on 75.5% of the test instances, despite substantially lower pointwise predictive…

logistics.title: DEG: Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet for Solving Vehicle Routing Problems
logistics.authors: Ni Zhang, Zhiqin Zhang, Ling Pan et al.
logistics.abstract: Traditional neural solvers for solving vehicle routing problems (VRPs) often suffer from limited solution diversity, motivating the development of Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet)-based models. However, the effectiveness of these models is frequently constrained by insufficient flow expansion in high-reward regions, limiting their ability to distribute probability across promising solution routes. Deeper exploration could yield superior results. Diffusion models, in contrast, provide stronger structural guidance for exploration. These two paradigms are naturally complementary: GFlowNet can supply edge-level signals for diffusion to embed, while diffusion can guide broader exploration. Leveraging this synergy, we propose Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet (DEG), a novel framework that integrates GFlowNet with a diffusion model to encourage richer flow expansion toward high-reward regions and derive higher-quality solutions. Specifically, DEG exploits GFlowNet's inherent diversity to generate edge-specific backward signals, applies the stochastic noise schedule of diffusion to perturb these signals, and then denoises them within the GFlowNet paradigm. To further improve scalability, we introduce a specialized decoder capable of dynamically adapting to diverse problem scales. Extensive experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, including instances with up to 10,000…

sales.title: An Essay on the Evolving Role of B2B Salespeople in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Challenges and Opportunities.
sales.authors: Pedro Mendonça Silva
sales.venue: International Journal of Marketing Communication and New Media
sales.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence in B2B sales is transforming processes, enhancing customer experiences, and reshaping sales roles. This essay examines AI’s impact, highlighting its benefits in efficiency, automation, and data-driven decision-making while addressing challenges such as cultural resistance and skill development. A conceptual model outlines key dimensions of AI-driven sales transformation. The study concludes that the future lies in a "Hybrid Model", where AI and human expertise coexist for innovation and competitive advantage. This essay can serve as a basis for future studies by proposing the conceptual model and suggesting empirical approaches to assess the impacts of AI on salespeople's performance. sales.title: AI-enabled social media: implications for salespeople, sales leadership, and sales organizations
sales.authors: Vishag A. Badrinarayanan, Christine Lai-Bennejean, Adam A. Rapp et al.
sales.venue: Journal of Personal Selling and Sales Management
sales.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded within social media, AI-enabled social media is increasingly changing how salespeople, sales leaders, and sales organizations engage with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders. Yet, sales research has largely focused on how sales actors use traditional social media with little emphasis on the implications of AI, a notable gap that also remains in the rapidly evolving research on AI in B2B sales. Thus, there is limited understanding of how embedding AI within social media alters the action possibilities available to sales actors. Drawing on affordance theory, we define AI-enabled social media and examine how AI alters and extends traditional social media affordances across external social media and enterprise social media (ESM), with implications for salespeople across the sales process, sales leadership across key leadership roles, and sales organizations across key organizational domains. We then discuss theoretical and managerial implications and develop a research agenda for advancing knowledge of AI-enabled social media in B2B sales.

sales.title: Penerapan Artificial Intelligence dalam Meningkatkan Penjualan B2B (Business To Business)
sales.authors: Andita Andita
sales.abstract: This study aims to deeply examine the role and impact of AI implementation in the B2B sales process, including implementation challenges. The method used is a qualitative approach with descriptive studies, through a literature review of scientific journals, industry reports, and relevant previous studies. The analysis results show that the application of AI in B2B sales not only improves the accuracy of marketing strategies and lead conversion, but also strengthens the concept of value co-creation through collaboration between salespeople and AI systems. Technologies such as machine learning, predictive analytics, and NLP-based chatbots have been proven to accelerate sales cycles, expand service reach, and increase productivity by up to 30%. However, implementation challenges remain, including limited digital infrastructure, a lack of competent human resources, and organizational resistance to technological transformation. Therefore, optimal AI integration requires institutional readiness, adaptive strategies, and continuous investment in technology and human resource development. These findings provide theoretical and practical contributions to the development of AI-based B2B sales strategies, particularly in the context of the digital industry in Indonesia. sales.title: Digital Transformation of B2B Sales Processes: Exploring Technology Adoption and Sales Performance Through a Qualitative Study
sales.authors: Slim Belaid, Marwa Ben Moallem
sales.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping business-to-business (B2B) sales processes through the growing use of customer relationship management systems, analytics dashboards, automation tools, digital communication channels, and predictive technologies. However, the performance effects of these tools remain insufficiently understood, particularly in complex B2B sales contexts where commercial work is relational, knowledge-intensive, and strongly dependent on organizational routines. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model, this study explores how B2B sales actors perceive, adopt, resist, and integrate digital tools into their daily commercial practices. Based on 18 semi-structured interviews with sales directors, sales managers, business development managers, and senior sales representatives, the study identifies a conditional process linking digital tool adoption to perceived sales performance. The findings show that adoption is mainly driven by perceived usefulness, while perceived ease of use depends less on interface simplicity than on compatibility with sales routines. Resistance emerges when tools create administrative duplication, threaten commercial autonomy, or remain poorly integrated into existing workflows. The study further shows that digital tools improve perceived sales performance indirectly, mainly through CRM integration, shared customer memory, data-driven…

sales.abstract: The article examines the impact of artificial intelligence on B2B sales processes, in particular, its role in increasing efficiency and predicting customer behavior. The article analyses the use of such technologies as natural language processing [NLP], machine learning [ML], computer vision, and chatbots. Particular attention is paid to the practical case of the American company Dell, which has achieved an increase in the conversion rate and optimization of the sales department with the help of Lattice Engines analytics. The study demonstrates that AI integration allows branding agencies to create more accurate customer profiles, automate routine tasks, and increase the level of interaction personalization. It is concluded that further development of predictive models and integration of AI with customer relationship management [CRM] systems are essential for achieving predictable results and enhancing companies' competitiveness. The study's novelty highlights the practical benefits of integrating AI into the B2B sales process, particularly its role in improving sales efficiency, personalization, and lead generation. sales.title: Managing the burnout process over time: A within-person examination of salesperson burnout
sales.authors: Dayle R. N. Childs, Belinda Dewsnap, Alec Pappas et al.
sales.abstract: Burnout is highly prevalent in the sales force, and is a serious concern for sales managers. Salesperson burnout is a process that requires management over time, yet no longitudinal within-person evidence exists regarding how salesperson burnout evolves over time or how to best manage the process. Using a 4-month repeated measures study of 171 B2B salespeople, we present the first longitudinal evidence of the within-person salesperson burnout process, and examine how key sales manager and salesperson variables can shape this process as it evolves. Results show some support for the burnout process, but find no link between diminished personal accomplishment and depersonalization. Moreover, positive feedback plays no role in mitigating burnout's evolution, while active coping and negative feedback mitigate the impacts of diminished personal accomplishment and depersonalization on emotional exhaustion, respectively. Our work presents tangible interventions that can help to reduce burnout as it evolves within salespeople over time.

sales.title: Emotional Intelligence Abilities and Work Engagement among Salespersons: A Conservation of Resources Theory Perspective from Germany’s Pharmaceutical Industry
sales.authors: Yahya Awadh Al-Nami, Amiya Bahaumik, Akram Mufareh Alshammakh
sales.venue: Journal of Business and Management Studies
sales.abstract: Sustaining salespersons’ work engagement has become a critical concern amid intensifying professional demands and increasing turnover within the German pharmaceutical B2B sector. Guided by the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examines how four distinct abilities of emotional intelligence—self-emotion appraisal, others’ emotion appraisal, emotion utilization, and emotion regulation—affect salespersons’ work engagement. Employing a quantitative design, data were collected from 340 pharmaceutical sales representatives in North Rhine-Westphalia and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that all four emotional intelligence abilities exert significant positive effects on work engagement, confirming the hypothesized relationships. Among these, the utilization and regulation of emotion emerged as the most influential predictors, underscoring their pivotal role in sustaining engagement within emotionally demanding sales environments. Overall, the four abilities of EI explained 68% of the variance in work engagement, affirming its value as a psychological resource that enhances motivational energy and mitigates emotional strain. sales.authors: Н. Є. Каличева, Maxim Kistanov

sales.abstract: In today's world, where global competition and the rapid development of technologies set a high pace of change, digital transformation is becoming a key success factor for many enterprises. In addition, the use of information technologies ensures cost optimization, improves communication between sellers and buyers. Digital transformation has become an integral part of modern business, and sales management is no exception. Under the influence of digital technologies, sales processes are undergoing significant changes, which requires enterprises to take new approaches and adapt to changing market conditions. Digitalization also significantly improves sales management by automating routine tasks, optimizing the use of data and creating a personalized approach to interaction with customers using tools such as CRM systems, analytics and artificial intelligence. This allows you to quickly respond to market changes, increase productivity, develop new sales markets and make informed decisions based on big data analysis. sales.authors: María Badenas-Boldó, Gloria Berenguer Contrí, Irene Gil Saura
sales.abstract: Purpose Sustainability research has led to growing interest in the impacts of current production and consumption models, driven by greater awareness among companies and consumers. In this context, this paper aims to analyse the extent to which sustainable practices implemented in commercial distribution function as a strategic enabler of salespeople's innovative behaviour. It also examines the impact of sales-service ambidexterity on this relationship, as well as the importance of value co-creation. Design/methodology/approach The authors propose a theoretical model based on existing literature. This model was tested using partial least squares regression analysis (PLS-SEM) on a sample of 272 salespeople (business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C)) from Spain and Portugal who work for a multinational building and decorating materials company. Findings The results show that sustainability dimensions are key factors driving salespeople's innovative service behaviour. Furthermore, sales-service ambidexterity and value co-creation significantly strengthen this relationship. As a result, these variables enhance the positive impact of sustainable practices on innovative behaviour. sales.title: Leveraging Network Marketing for B2B Sales: Strategies, Challenges, and Market Impact
sales.authors: Dr. Kamal Kishor Pandey, Dr. Himanshu Dargan, Dr. Rahul, Ms. Nidhi Varshney
sales.abstract: Network marketing is starting to make a name for itself in the business-to-business (B2B) sector, despite its more common association with consumer sales. In this article, we take a look at how network marketing helps companies increase their sales, strengthen their relationships, and broaden their reach in the market. Some of the tactics covered include multi-tiered distribution structures, referral-based sales, and digital marketing integration. Furthermore, the research highlights significant obstacles, such as trust concerns, regulatory limitations, and the intricacy of B2B decision-making. Surveys, interviews, and case studies of companies using network marketing for business-to-business transactions make up the study's mixed-method research methodology. The findings indicate that while network marketing can enhance sales performance and market reach, its success is contingent on credibility, technological support, & ethical practices. Companies that effectively navigate these challenges by leveraging digital tools and fostering transparency can gain a competitive advantage in the B2B landscape. In addition to providing useful advice for companies thinking about using network marketing to expand, this study adds to the expanding body of literature on alternate business-to-business sales models. sales.authors: Narek Halstian
sales.venue: The American Journal of Management and Economics Innovations
sales.abstract: This article substantiates the necessity of transitioning to an integrated digital sales ecosystem as a key factor of competitiveness. The relevance of the study is determined by the rapid growth of electronic commerce and the approach of the online channel share to 20% in global retail, which renders traditional methods of sales management economically inefficient. The author emphasizes that digital transformation should be regarded not as a one-off project but as a continuously accelerating positive feedback loop requiring end-to-end integration of CRM, POS, BI, and ERP/OMS. The objective of the study is to systematize and analyze contemporary digital solutions applied to sales management in the retail business, as well as to identify the mechanisms of their interaction and their impact on key operational indicators. The methodological basis comprised a comparative analysis of reports by UNCTAD, Emarketer, McKinsey, Intellias, and leading industry research, as well as content analysis of practical case studies and statistical data. The theoretical part examines the four layers of the sales tech stack, while the empirical part provides examples of the implementation of AI modules, predictive analytics, and omnichannel platforms. sales.title: Leveraging AI for Go-To-Market Efficiency: A Framework for Product-Led Growth in B2B Sales Teams
sales.authors: Adish Rai
sales.venue: International Journal on Science and Technology
sales.abstract: Product-led growth has emerged as a dominant model in B2B software, where users adopt products through self-service trials before engaging with sales teams. This shift creates challenges for traditional sales organizations that must identify high-value accounts, prioritize expansion opportunities, and personalize outreach based on product usage signals rather than manual research alone. This paper presents a practical framework for B2B sales teams adopting AI-assisted workflows in a product-led environment. We describe how usage data, firmographic enrichment, and language models combine to surface qualified accounts, generate contextual outreach, and support account planning. The framework covers signal identification, data integration patterns, AI-assisted messaging, and operational guardrails. While implementation examples reference common platforms, the approach remains portable to any stack with equivalent capabilities.

sales.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in the B2B Sales Funnel
sales.authors: David Fehrenbach, Carolina Herrando, Benjamin Österle

AI can support and even take over the tasks of managers and salespeople related to data-driven decisions. However, studies are lacking concerning the B2B sales problems that can be solved with AI and the AI types that can be applied to certain tasks. Moreover, the emergence of generative AI has disrupted this research area, offering new opportunities and challenges. This study therefore seeks to answer the question: What is the current state of knowledge of AI in B2B sales (regarding consensus definitions, theoretical grounding application, sales problems for which AI is used, and AI techniques and models applied at each stage of the B2B sales funnel)?.Methodology To explore this, we conduct a framework-based literature review of current AI applications for B2B sales problems. sales.title: Self-Set Goals and Sales Performance: A Field Experiment on Goal Setting and CRM-Enabled Feedback in B2B Sales
sales.authors: Sophie Kuhlemann
sales.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
sales.abstract: Digital feedback tools are increasingly relevant in the workplace, yet many recent advances lack features that genuinely enhance employee motivation, particularly in sales environments where individual performance directly shapes organizational outcomes. Drawing on goal-setting theory, this study investigates how self-set goals and adaptive, CRM-informed feedback influence salespeople’s performance in a B2B context. To this end, we propose a six-month field study within a B2B organization in which we enable employees to set, monitor, and adjust personal goals and provide them with data-driven feedback. With that, our research aims to contribute to the literature on goal setting, feedback, and motivational technologies in the workplace. Practically, our findings seek to guide organizations in designing IS-enabled interventions that enhance salesperson engagement and improve overall performance.

sales.title: Peran Integrasi AI Dalam Meningkatkan Penjualan Di era Digital 5.0
sales.authors: Baramadya ., Muhammad Wisnu Girindratama, Deyka Aguilika
sales.abstract: Sales management is undergoing a digital transformation driven by AI tools like Seamless AI and Einstein (Sales AI), which are reshaping B2B customer journeys. Grounded in dynamic capabilities theory, this study examines how B2B firms integrate AI into sales processes. We propose that marketing agility—defined by proactivity, responsiveness, and speed—mediates the relationship between AI adoption and sales team performance in uncertain markets. Furthermore, the research investigates how marketing influence and internal organizational climate moderate these dynamics. Data were gathered from B2B sales managers at firms with over 100 employees and at least $1 million in annual revenue. The findings highlight that strategic AI adoption must align with marketing agility to effectively boost firm performance. This study contributes to emerging literature on the facilitators of agility within the B2B sector.

sales.title: Analysis and improvement of sales management through CRM and simulation utilisation
sales.authors: Samer Abaddi
sales.abstract: This study aims to analyse the current sales processes in X company and to model them using Simul8 software. Furthermore, it develops a strategic scene depending on the situational analysis. The study’s approach aimed to define the sales channels by conducting five interviews with managers in sales departments in different regions of the world. This made it easy to define and map the sales pipeline, which assisted in optimisation using the SWOT analysis, confrontation matrix, and simulation. The study revealed that the current sales operations take a long time, and the work of the sales department intersects with many internal and external operations, in addition to its reliance on manual work to a large extent. The study recommended a model towards automating processes and integrating Customer Relationship Management (CRM) with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) in the future. The study identified the challenges for the integration of the new systems and recommended training employees, the possibility of opening digital stores to sell medical equipment directly to customers, and the use of analytical CRM in sales management. The implications of these improvements, demonstrate significant enhancements in operational efficiency, reduced cycle times, and increased profitability, positioning the company for greater competitiveness.

sales.title: Sales Force Automation, Customer Relationship Management Systems: Implications For Customer Value Creation In Telecommunication Firms In Port Harcourt

A multiple regression analysis was performed to test how customer value creation is influenced by sales force automation and customer relationship management. The analysis results showed that customer value creation is positively affected by sales force automation as well as customer relationship management. The findings indicate that the telecommunications companies' ability to develop value for customers is enhanced by the adoption and effective utilization of these technological systems. From the analysis, the null hypotheses were all rejected. These results affirm that the combination of customer relationship management and sales force automation systems increases customer value creation in the telecommunications companies. sales.authors: Göran Svensson, Rocío Rodríguez, Nils M. Høgevold

sales.abstract: Purpose Sales force automation (SFA) tools have become central to managing international selling, yet evidence on their adoption is scattered across theories, contexts and methods. This study reviews and integrates SFA adoption research to explain how individual, organisational and technological factors jointly shape outcomes in cross-border and culturally diverse marketing environments. sales.title: Adaptive Sales Strategies In Competitive Markets: The Role Of Sales Management In Sustainable Business Growth
sales.authors: Iryna M. Chaika
sales.abstract: The period of market volatility between 2022 and 2024 revealed substantial weaknesses in the ability of many sales organizations to respond effectively to competitive disruption and rapidly changing customer behavior. Strategies that had previously generated acceptable results under relatively stable market conditions proved insufficient when purchasing cycles shortened, buying criteria changed, and competitive pressures intensified. Industry evidence indicates that B2B sales performance deteriorated significantly during this period, with win rates declining to approximately 21% and only 29% of sales representatives achieving their sales quotas. Simultaneously, organizations experienced longer decision-making processes, lower conversion rates, and reductions in deal value, highlighting the necessity of more adaptive and strategically responsive sales management approaches. The subject of this study is market-responsive sales management and the organizational mechanisms that enable firms to adapt their sales strategies to conditions of environmental uncertainty and competitive turbulence. sales.title: What Competencies Should I be Teaching in my Introductory Business-to-Business Sales Course in the Age of Artificial Intelligence?
sales.authors: Carlos Valdéz
sales.abstract: The present study investigates a current question among sales educators: What competencies should I be teaching in my introductory business-to-business (B2B) sales course in the age of artificial intelligence (AI)? Using a mixed-methods approach, data were collected from seven interviews with sales managers and 13 interviews with alumni, along with an online survey of 157 sales professionals. Based on these data, the contribution presents five relevant findings about which competencies to teach. First, the findings highlight the importance of active listening and salesperson authenticity. Second, they emphasize an increased focus on discovery and the need for diagnosis rather than simply closing. Third, the role of AI emerges as one of augmentation, not replacement, of the salesperson’s human judgment. Fourth, participants identified knowing when not to use AI as the most critical AI competency. Fifth, the findings reveal a data privacy paradox: Although 77% of sales professionals avoid using AI when managing confidential data, data privacy ranked lowest among sales curriculum priorities. Together, these findings suggest ways to revise the competencies taught in introductory sales courses, potentially closing the gap between what is taught and what employers expect in the age of AI.

And while expectations about XR technologies are high, their specific impact on personal selling and sales interactions in business-to-business (B2B) contexts remains unclear. Against this background, the authors provide insight into the unique benefits through which XR technologies may contribute to salesperson performance and the conditions under which these benefits are likely. sales.abstract: Increasing requirements for sustainable development, environmental transparency, and corporate social responsibility are driving the transformation of approaches to sales management in enterprises. The purpose of the article is to develop a conceptual model for integrating corporate social responsibility into sales management strategies and to substantiate the logic of its influence on key sales performance indicators, taking into account industry specifics. sales.abstract: The rapid growth of India's economy, projected to be the third largest by 2027, underscores the critical role of Big Data Analytics (BDA) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing business performance, particularly in the Business-to-Business (B2B) market. This study examines the impact of BDA and AI on perceived sales performance (PSP) in the Indian B2B context, with Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology as a mediator. Despite the recognized potential of these technologies, there is a paucity of research exploring their combined effect on sales performance and the mediating role of CRM in emerging markets. A quantitative approach was employed, utilizing a survey with a structured questionnaire distributed to 393 B2B sales professionals across India, selected via convenience and snowball sampling.
